## Overview

The emerald ash borer, *Agrilus planipennis*, a beetle from Asia found near
Detroit in 2002, has killed hundreds of millions of ash trees in North
America. Its larvae feed in the phloem under the bark, girdling the tree.
@Mercader2011 asked how far an infestation spreads from a single point, and
how that depends on where the ash is and on how the females choose where to
lay. Their model is a coupled map lattice: cells of 50 m hold amounts of ash
phloem and numbers of beetles, which spread, breed and eat phloem each year.

This implementation is a **reproduction** of the model's two behaviours in
its published code, and an inferred version of a third; it reproduces the
source's radii of infestation year by year.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using EcologicalCellularAutomata
using CellularAutomataCore
using Plots
using Random
using Statistics
```

## The model

Each year:

- adults emerge from larvae that took one year, and from those that took two;
- they disperse from their cell by a negative exponential kernel (`b = 0.037`
  per metre), normalised over the cells within 50 cells; with **avoidance**,
  cells without phloem are treated as 1.8 km further away;
- each female lays `r0 = 10.35` female offspring, as far as the phloem allows
  at `C = 0.0113` m² per larva, which the larvae eat;
- a share `-0.194 ln(x) + 0.986` of the larvae, `x` larvae per m² of phloem,
  take two years to develop.

The model is deterministic. The landscape is surrounded by a border of 2
cells where dispersing beetles are lost, as in the source's code.

```{julia}
prob = problem(:emerald_ash_borer)
size(prob.u0.phloem), sum(prob.u0.phloem[3:(end - 2), 3:(end - 2)])
```

The landscape is 205 × 205 cells (about 10 × 10 km) holding 8,405,000 m² of
phloem, here spread evenly, 200 m² a cell. One hundred adults start at its
centre.

## Spread year by year

```{julia}
function spread(; years=15, kwargs...)
    integ = init(problem(:emerald_ash_borer; years, kwargs...); save_everystep=false)
    out = [eab_spread(integ.u)]
    while integ.t < years
        step!(integ)
        push!(out, eab_spread(integ.u))
    end
    return out, integ.u
end
avoid, final = spread()
standard, _ = spread(; behaviour=:standard)
Int.(getfield.(avoid, :radius))
```

These are the radii of infestation, from year 0 to year 15, with avoidance:
the farthest cell from the origin holding at least one larva. They are those
of the source's Fig. 9, year by year.

```{julia}
p1 = plot(0:15, [getfield.(standard, :radius) getfield.(avoid, :radius)]; marker=:circle,
          ms=3, lw=2, label=["standard" "avoidance"], xlabel="year", ylabel="radius (m)",
          legend=:topleft)
plot!(p1, 0:15, [getfield.(standard, :median) getfield.(avoid, :median)]; ls=:dash,
      color=[1 2], label=["median, standard" "median, avoidance"])
p2 = plot(0:15, [getfield.(standard, :beetles) getfield.(avoid, :beetles)] ./ 1e6;
          lw=2, marker=:circle, ms=3, label=["standard" "avoidance"], xlabel="year",
          ylabel="beetles (millions)", legend=:topleft)
plot(p1, p2; layout=(1, 2), size=(850, 320), left_margin=4Plots.mm,
     bottom_margin=4Plots.mm)
```

Without avoidance, larvae fill the cells near the origin, eat them out, and
the beetles emerging there keep laying in empty cells nearby. With avoidance
they fly over the eaten-out core to fresh ash, so the infestation spreads
further and holds more beetles: after 15 years 1350 m and 5.5 million here,
against 1200 m and 3.9 million without (the source: 1350 m and about 5.3
million, 1200 m and about 3.8 million).

```{julia}
heatmap(final.phloem[3:(end - 2), 3:(end - 2)][63:143, 63:143]; aspect_ratio=1, c=:YlGn,
        title="phloem left after 15 years, central 4 × 4 km", titlefontsize=10,
        xticks=false, yticks=false, size=(420, 380))
```

## The arrangement of ash

The source compares three landscapes with the same total phloem: even,
clumped (blocks of 5 × 5 cells separated by gaps of 5 empty cells) and random
(cells holding 0 to 400 m² at random).

```{julia}
plot([heatmap(eab_environment(k; rng=Random.Xoshiro(1))[73:133, 73:133]; aspect_ratio=1,
              c=:YlGn, title=string(k), titlefontsize=10, xticks=false, yticks=false,
              colorbar=false)
      for k in (:homogeneous, :clumped, :random)]...; layout=(1, 3), size=(800, 270))
```

The central 3 × 3 km of each. Fifteen years in each landscape, with each
behaviour, and the source's values read from its Figs 4 and 5 (radius in m,
beetles in millions):

```{julia}
source = Dict((:homogeneous, :standard) => (1200, 3.8),
              (:homogeneous, :avoidance) => (1350, 5.3),
              (:homogeneous, :resource_bias) => (1350, 5.3),
              (:clumped, :standard) => (750, 1.0), (:clumped, :avoidance) => (1650, 9.0),
              (:clumped, :resource_bias) => (2600, 10.5),
              (:random, :standard) => (1200, 3.8), (:random, :avoidance) => (1500, 6.2),
              (:random, :resource_bias) => (2050, 11.0))
cases = [(e, b) for e in (:homogeneous, :clumped, :random)
         for b in (:standard, :avoidance, :resource_bias)]
finals = fetch.([Threads.@spawn eab_spread(solve(problem(:emerald_ash_borer; environment=e,
                                                         behaviour=b); saveat=15).u[end])
                 for (e, b) in cases])
[(environment=e, behaviour=b, radius=r.radius, beetles=round(r.beetles / 1e6; digits=2),
  source=source[(e, b)]) for ((e, b), r) in zip(cases, finals)]
```

Standard and avoidance reproduce the source in every landscape. Clumping
hinders a beetle that does not avoid empty ground: most of its offspring land
in the gaps, so in the clumped landscape it spreads only 750 m. A beetle that
avoids empty ground spreads furthest there, as each clump is eaten out and
the beetles fly to the next. The source's third behaviour, a bias towards
cells rich in phloem, is inferred here from its description; it reproduces
the homogeneous result, and spreads further than avoidance in the other two
landscapes, as in the source, but less far.

## How many founders

The source compares 100 and 1,000 founders, and reports the difference in
the final number of beetles as 67.5, 21.8 and 10.3% in the clumped,
homogeneous and random landscapes:

```{julia}
envs = (:clumped, :homogeneous, :random)
founders = fetch.([Threads.@spawn eab_spread(solve(problem(:emerald_ash_borer; environment=e,
                                                           founders=f); saveat=15).u[end])
                   for e in envs for f in (100, 1000)])
[(environment=e, beetles_100=round(founders[2k - 1].beetles / 1e6; digits=2),
  beetles_1000=round(founders[2k].beetles / 1e6; digits=2),
  difference=round(100 * (founders[2k].beetles - founders[2k - 1].beetles) /
                   founders[2k].beetles; digits=1),
  radius_1000=founders[2k].radius)
 for (k, e) in enumerate(envs)]
```

In the homogeneous and random landscapes, ten times as many founders give an
infestation about 20% and 8% larger after 15 years (21.8% and 10.3% in the
source), far from ten times larger, as the phloem near the origin limits it.
In the clumped landscape the number of beetles swings from year to year, as
the clumps are eaten out and the beetles fly to the next, and at year 15 the
run with 1,000 founders happens to be in a trough; the source, whose clumped
runs also oscillate strongly, finds 67.5% more.
